status: REFERENCE AND EVENT HISTORIES BOUND; SENSITIVITY IS CONDITIONAL; 1H-30M REFINEMENT MISSED FROZEN DECAY TOLERANCE; 20M-16M40S REFINEMENT PASSED
scope: Numerical integration and deterministic history controls driven by one sampled 1M fixed-source reference transport run. Not empirical validation or reactor qualification.

event_control.interpretation: Service events are triggered by point estimates from sampled component flux means; tally standard errors are retained in driving_rates but are not propagated into event times, fluences, or threshold-crossing probabilities. The 31 blanket replacement events and absence of a sampled-mean magnet trip are therefore conditional control outputs, not evidence about true hardware exposure or lifetime. The 49.6% magnet flux relative standard error is material to this interpretation.

sensitivity.interpretation: This grid varies only the stated authored recovery, processing-delay, and service-trigger assumptions with the same transport point means. Positive and negative net-energy point estimates both occur; neither sign is uncertainty-qualified or a prediction. It is not an uncertainty distribution.

time_refinement.criterion: relative cumulative production/burn/full-power/fusion-energy changes <=1e-4; final available inventory and decay changes <=1e-4 kg; identical event-kind sequence and event timing shift <= coarse step.

one_hour_to_thirty_minutes.failure_reason: decay change exceeds the frozen 1e-4 kg absolute tolerance; net electricity is cancellation-sensitive and changes about 0.37% relative, so no sign-based inference is supported.

twenty_minutes_to_sixteen_minutes_forty_.criterion_note: pass at these fine integration resolutions for this fixed mean-rate scenario; it does not constrain Monte Carlo, nuclear-data, or model uncertainty and does not make the failed 1h result pass.

uncertainty_treatment: The history engine deterministically integrates transport response means. It carries each input response standard error unchanged in its driving-rate provenance, but does not propagate tally covariance, Monte Carlo uncertainty, half-life uncertainty, or model discrepancy into exposures, threshold-event timing, or net-energy uncertainty. Zero mean/zero standard error for a component with no sampled tracks is retained as a finite sampled result, not interpreted as proof of zero true flux or as an upper bound. Derived outcome labels are therefore conditional on these point means.
